learned: Run on pipeline v3 (--v3), from this session: the tools run here, the helpers each an Opus subagent in a fresh context.

Plan writer (1 subagent): given plan-brief.md, the lesson folder, 00_beginner.png and the technique file. Wrote 23 steps in 9 stages, 15 units, 14 renders, 8 mixes. Asked once more after check, with check's problem only, to merge Golden orange into Rust brown (fitted to the same color); it did, and noted the ginger-locks step's words now lay the block-in's own paint.

Chain checker (1 subagent, twice): given chain-check.md and chain/looks. Read 14 looks and marked none; erase run again after the merge rewrote the looks, so a fresh checker read them again and marked none.

Stage writers (9 subagents, then 9 more): given only their words/stage-NN folder. packets rewrote every folder after the merge, so all nine stages were written again by fresh writers. Round 1: 108 claims, 8 failed, 5 stages fixed once. Round 2: 110 claims, 7 failed, 4 stages fixed once; then 3 writers sent back once for paints their words named that their steps don't list. Final: 103 claims, 0 failed, 0 sentences taken out.
erase asked again by itself twice for the sunset clouds left standing (2.1% of the canvas) and kept them: faint streaks on a sky, a known limit.

Four paints were fitted 27 to 32 Lab units from the plan's color (Dusky rose, Golden orange, Rosy nose, Nose pink). Golden orange then merged into Rust brown at check's request; the other three stay as known problems.

Several writers said the plan's after lines disagree with the pictures: the sky runs to the bottom edge where the plan says the bottom is bare (the same fault as the floating island), and the dark grass doesn't hide the cow's legs.
Re-running packets after a plan change throws away every stage's words, so a merge at check costs a whole second round of writers.
notes.read: A shaggy ginger highland cow faces us in tall meadow grass at sunset, mountains and a strip of loch behind, the low sun on the right lighting the coat's edge. The lesson is about the coat: a flat shape first, then shade, locks and a gold rim, with the grass laid over the legs last. Hard parts: hair without single strands, and a face mostly hidden under the fringe.
notes.order: Back to front, as the technique says: sky, clouds, far mountains and lake, hills and meadow, bushes, then the cow (block-in, shade, horns, locks), the grass in front of its legs, the rim light, and the face last as the final details. Planned by the v3 plan writer in a fresh context.

stages.name: Blend the sunset sky
steps: Inside the outlined area. It reaches all four edges of the canvas.
Paints, top to bottom: Sky blue, Cream gold, then Pale gold.
Mix enough Cream gold for this step and steps 6 and 20; cover it between them.
Mix enough Pale gold for this step and steps 3 and 19; cover it between them.
Brush: 1 inch flat. Load: Creamy paint. An even coat.
Start with the darkest color and stroke side to side. Without rinsing, pick up the next lighter color and paint below it. Then stroke back up over the join several times.
It should leave soft side-to-side bands of blue and gold over the whole canvas, with a soft join where two wet colors meet.
Watch out: Blending after the paint has started to drag. Acrylic sets in minutes, and scrubbing setting paint lifts it and leaves streaks. Fix: stop as soon as it drags.
Let it dry, then blend a new thin layer on top.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

technique_picks.technique_why: A sunset landscape with one big shaggy animal in front is the classic back-to-front paint-along: sky, mountains and hills go on in big easy shapes, and the cow's coat builds from flat shape to long locks in plain repeated strokes.

parts.name: The sunset sky
parts.why: A smooth blue-to-gold sunset blended wet in one go, run down past the mountains.

parts.name: The sunset clouds
parts.why: Soft streaks of peach and rose with gold tops, dry-brushed onto the dry sky.

parts.name: The far blue mountains
parts.why: Two ranges of distant mountains with no texture, the far one paler and more violet.

parts.name: The glimpse of lake
parts.why: A thin pale strip of water at the far right where the hills dip, laid in with level strokes; it is too small to need ripples.

parts.name: The green hills and meadow
parts.why: The green slopes behind the cow are a field seen from a distance: a base, then darker bands along the slopes, no texture.

parts.name: The dark bushes on the hills
parts.why: Small far bushes and shrubs dotted over the slopes; only the dark dab, since far trees get no detail.

parts.name: The Highland cow
parts.why: A long-haired cow whose coat hangs in locks over a darker body, lit from behind, with its eyes under a fringe: exactly this element.
parts.left_out: Single hairs, fine wisps at the coat's edge, and the eyes, which stay hidden under the fringe as in the finish.

parts.name: The cow's shadows

parts.name: The cow's horns
